blocking.section: Distributed state catalog > State client and RZ-STS error codes
blocking.issue: The RZ-STS registry fixes every code at 503 before commit. That contradicts pack 8.10, where a closed failure in a response Phase before commit replaces the response with 502. A State Store call can fail in a response Phase: WASM plugin system allows `state_get` in any Phase before commit, and a Plugin Policy may run in onUpstreamResponseHeaders or onResponse.
blocking.evidence: Line 332: "All codes return 503 before commit in the [Data plane](03-data-plane.md#error-response-format) format." Lines 336-340: every row has Status "503". Pack 8.10: "A response Phase before commit | Replace the response with 502". 05-wasm-plugin-system.md line 176: "`state_get` ... Before commit, never `onChunk`".
blocking.fix: Line 332 should read: "Before commit, a code returns 503 in a request Phase and 502 in a response Phase (pack 8.10), in the Data plane format." Change the Status column of RZ-STS-001 to RZ-STS-005 to "503; 502 in a response Phase".

blocking.issue: The divided-Quota example puts a Bundle kind (`Consumer`) and control-plane-only kinds (`Environment`, `Cluster`) in one YAML stream with no file boundary. Loaded as one Bundle file, this is RZ-CFG-017 under pack section 3 (Scope: control plane only) and the Configuration model, which keeps `Environment` and `Cluster` in `control/` outside the Bundle.
blocking.evidence: Lines 434-476: one ```yaml fence holding `kind: Consumer`, then `---`, `kind: Environment` (prod-eu), `kind: Environment` (prod-us) and `kind: Cluster` (prod-us-east). 02-configuration-model.md line 594: "`Environment` and `Cluster` are rejected inside a Bundle (RZ-CFG-017)". Line 1441: "`control/environments.yaml` and `control/clusters.yaml` sit outside the Bundle and are applied to Ruralz Control".
blocking.fix: Split the sketch into two fences, each with a one-line lead-in naming its file, as the Configuration model does: `consumers/partner-acme.yaml` (Bundle) holding only the Consumer, and `control/environments.yaml` (outside the Bundle, applied to Ruralz Control) holding the two Environments and the Cluster.

blocking.issue: The Token Budget healthy-closed bound drops two terms that AI/LLM gateway (a depends_on document and the owner of the bound) includes: extra attempts and hidden reasoning. As written the bound is tighter than the owner's bound, so it contradicts it.
blocking.evidence: Line 359: "| Token Budget | Healthy, `closed` | Overshoot at most the sum of input-estimate errors, SM-10, owned by [AI/LLM gateway](06-ai-llm-gateway.md#settlement) (hypothesis) |". 06-ai-llm-gateway.md line 326: "overshoots a budget by at most the sum of input-estimate errors across concurrent requests (hypothesis; SM-10 ...), plus (attempts - 1) x R per concurrent request ... plus, while OQ-ai-llm-gateway-17 is open, hidden reasoning above C on `gemini` and `ollama`."
blocking.fix: Replace the Bound cell with: "Overshoot at most the sum of input-estimate errors plus (attempts − 1) × R per concurrent request, plus hidden reasoning above C on `gemini` and `ollama` while OQ-ai-llm-gateway-17 is open; SM-10, owned by AI/LLM gateway (hypothesis)".

blocking.issue: The fail-open bound for derived ceilings leaves out the one-token-per-Node floor that Traffic management and resilience applies to fail-open buckets. When `requests` < N_published / 2 the stated bound is too low. For example, 10 per window on 100 Nodes gives 20 under the formula, but 09 admits 100.
blocking.evidence: Line 353: "| Rate Limit, fail-open | Derived ceiling, OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-16 option (b) | At most N_serving / N_published × 2 × `requests` per aligned window (target) |". 09 line 264: "each derived-ceiling bucket holds max(1, 2 × `requests` / N_published) tokens per epoch-aligned window". 09 line 479: "Unfloored buckets admit N_serving / N_published × 2 × limit per aligned window, one token per Node at least".
blocking.fix: Change the Bound to "At most N_serving × max(1, 2 × `requests` / N_published) per aligned window (target)".

blocking.section: Distributed state catalog > Distributed rate limits; Consistency and accuracy bounds
blocking.issue: The document claims per-request GCRA keeps the Cell limit exact while the State Store is healthy. In the same section it recommends OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-20 option (a), which this document owns. Under that option, first-seen keys past the budget are admitted local-only, without GCRA, at up to N × ceiling for 10 s. The healthy-State-Store bounds table has no row for that case, so the bound it presents is wrong under the recommended design.
blocking.evidence: Line 287: "GCRA runs per admitted request ... keeping the Cell limit exact while the State Store is healthy." Line 291: "This document recommends ... option (a) of -20". Line 350: "| Rate Limit | Healthy State Store | At most `requests` per `window` sustained ...". 09 line 214: "past it, as OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-20 proposes, a 10 s local-only entry (target) at the per-Node ceiling ... without GCRA". 09 line 483: "later keys local-only at N × ceiling in their own segment".
blocking.fix: On line 287, after "exact", add: "under option (c) of OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-20, the conforming behavior until OQ-scalability-and-distributed-state-11 closes". Add a bounds row: "| Rate Limit | Healthy, first-seen key past the budget, OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-20 option (a) (proposed) | At most N_serving × ceiling per window while its 10 s local-only entry lives (target) |".

blocking.issue: The table calls itself "the complete inventory of in-memory per-Node state", but it leaves out per-Node state that this document and its dependencies define. That fails acceptance criterion 3 and the document's own rule that new per-Node state needs a row.
blocking.evidence: Line 50: "This table is the complete inventory of in-memory per-Node state; new per-Node state needs a row here before it ships." Missing: the State client's per-shard connections, breakers and 8,192 in-flight call slots (this document, line 330); the Response Cache `Vary`-name LRU per URI (09 line 376: "cached per URI in a bounded LRU"); `/tap` buffers (03 line 131: "Post-commit writes, `/tap` buffers | Fixed capacity"); the first-seen GCRA budget counter (09 line 214); and the Semantic Cache per-Node caps on concurrent embedding calls and store rate (06 lines 459, 465).
blocking.fix: Add rows, each with Bound, Rebuilt from and Why losing it is safe. State client connections, breakers and in-flight slots: 2 pipelined plus 8 dedicated per shard and 8,192 calls (target); rebuilt by redial and `SCRIPT LOAD`; a restart only re-closes breakers. `Vary`-name LRU: bounded; relearned on a miss; misses only. `/tap` and telemetry export buffers: fixed capacity; rebuilt from nothing; lost samples only. First-seen budget and Semantic Cache per-Node caps: counters; reset; a restart only restarts warm-up.
